answers.rationale: Flag to 100% at 17:20 with one uncached per-item request per tile (E08); per-item rate rose 1,400 -> 9,100/s while listing views were flat (E09, E11); replicas saturated by 17:32 (E07). The product-team estimate (E10) is contradicted by measured traffic.
Errors are timeouts waiting on inventory-service, which is itself waiting on the database; restarting checkout pods produced only a transient dip.
Pool waits are where the delay appears, but the primary is CPU-saturated; a previous pool increase under saturation worsened write latency. The pool is a symptom location, not the binding constraint.
The upgrade was uneventful at normal load for 40 hours, but replay throughput on 15.8 has never been measured at elevated load, so neither reduced nor unchanged throughput is established.
Reservation writes are unchanged; redirected reads began at 17:34-17:35 and primary saturation at 17:38, before the bot spike at 17:50.
Per-item rate increase after 17:20 coincides with replica CPU rising to 99% by 17:32, with no change in listing views.
Lag stayed at 0.1-0.3 s for 40 hours and rose to 3-8 s only after replica CPU reached 99%.
The guard redirects reads when lag exceeds 2 s; redirected reads rose from zero as lag exceeded 3 s.
Primary write latency and pool waits exceed the 2 s checkout timeout.
Timeouts began at 17:40 and persisted after the four-minute loss cleared.
Saturation preceded the bot spike, so the bots are not the origin, but whether login traffic touches this primary at all was never established; any contribution is undetermined.
Adds concurrency to a CPU-saturated primary; the only in-case precedent shows write latency worsening sharply.
Would lower the recorded timeout-error rate while connections are held longer; mobile clients abandon at 5 s and retry while abandoned work continues, adding load to the saturated primary.
Removes the uncached per-item read volume at its origin while keeping the feature; batch endpoint has a 96% CDN hit ratio.
Low-risk capacity at a mediator, but not available before the 20:00 peak and does not remove the origin load.
Moves the failure from latency to correctness: replicas lag 3-8 s, the range that previously caused overselling.
Checkout-service is not the origin; the prior restart gave a transient dip only.
Removes the origin load immediately through the flag.

missingInformation: Replica replay throughput on Postgres 15.8 under elevated load.
Whether the login service's session store shares the inventory primary.
hardness.reasoningChain: stock-badges flag to 100% with uncached per-item calls (E08) -> per-item rate 6.5x with flat page views (E09, E11) -> replica CPU 99% (E07) -> lag above 2 s (E07) -> lag guard redirects reads to primary (E05, E06) -> primary CPU saturation with unchanged writes (E03) -> pool waits and reservation latency above the 2 s timeout (E02, E01).
constructTraps: Treating pool wait (E02) as the leverage point rather than the place where upstream load becomes visible.
Raising the timeout, which improves the error metric while increasing load.
Disabling the lag guard, which removes the primary load by moving the failure into overselling.
Treating added replicas as the fix when it cannot arrive before the peak and leaves the origin intact.
